Summarize population marginal coefficients from a joint covariate model

Source: R/marginal-analysis.R
catmech_marginal_summary.Rd

Summarizes the population regression of the true measurement on the original continuous predictors from a fitted multivariate Gaussian cluster model. Predictor means and covariances are estimated jointly with the measurement model, allowing site effects in the measurement and predictors to be correlated.

Usage

catmech_marginal_summary(
  result,
  level = 0.95,
  formula = NULL,
  response = NULL,
  covariates = NULL
)

Arguments

result

A converged result from [catmech_reference()] with `cluster_model = "joint_marginal"`. An all-reference shortcut contains no fitted parameter posterior and cannot be summarized by this function.

level

Central posterior credible interval probability, strictly between zero and one.

formula

Optional two-sided additive linear formula with an intercept (for example `outcome ~ recorded + x`) naming a response and covariates from the audited value (`spec$value`, mapped to the true measurement `T`) and the complete numeric predictors in `spec$predictors`. Use this when the audited measurement is an analysis predictor and the scientific outcome was included in `predictors` during [catmech_reference()]. Cannot be combined with `response` or `covariates`.

response

Optional name of the population regression response, either `spec$value` or one of `spec$predictors`. Defaults to `spec$value`.

covariates

Optional character vector of population regression covariates chosen from `c(spec$value, spec$predictors)` excluding `response`. When `response` is supplied and `covariates` is `NULL`, all remaining modeled variables in `c(spec$value, spec$predictors)` are used.

Value

A data frame with `term`, `estimate`, `posterior_sd`, `lower`, `upper`, `level`, `rhat`, `ess_bulk`, `ess_tail`, `mcse_mean`, `mcse_lower`, `mcse_upper`, `draws`, `iterations`, `chains`, and `interpretation`.

Details

The model is `(T,W,X) = mu + b_site + e`, with independent Gaussian site and row vectors having unrestricted covariance matrices `Psi` and `Sigma`. For every posterior draw, let `V = Psi + Sigma`. By default, the marginal slopes are `solve(V[X,X], V[X,T])` and the intercept is `mu[T] - mu[X]' beta`, transformed back to the original units. When `formula`, `response` or `covariates` selects another modeled response `Y` and covariate set `P` from `(T, X)` (excluding the noisy proxy `W`), the marginal slopes are `solve(V[P,P], V[P,Y])` and the intercept is `mu[Y] - mu[P]' beta` in original units. This allows the audited measurement `T` to serve as an analysis predictor (`Y ~ T + X`) without the unaudited-cluster slope attenuation of the moment model. This is the population linear regression for an individual sampled under the model, not a within-site coefficient or the OLS slope of the completed cohort. Site size must be noninformative. The Gaussian covariate model is an additional assumption; categorical, incomplete and deterministically related predictors are not supported by this engine.

Each site/row covariance is factored into predictor covariance, regression of the two measurements on predictors, and conditional measurement covariance. The two covariance blocks have Huang–Wand priors with half-t(2) marginal standard deviations and scale `sqrt(joint_control$prior_scale)` in empirically standardized units. Those properties do not apply to the reconstructed full covariance. Regression matrices have proper zero-mean matrix-normal priors, with row covariance `regression_scale^2 * I` (default scale ten) and column covariance equal to the conditional measurement covariance. The population mean prior is flat. Credible intervals remain conditional on these distributional and reference-selection assumptions. They are not cluster-robust intervals and do not establish robustness to arbitrary contextual effects, nonlinear associations or informative cluster sizes.

Every retained draw from every chain is used independently of `m`. Equal-tailed quantiles use R quantile type 7. Original-unit coefficient diagnostics are recomputed: R-hat at most 1.05 and both bulk/tail ESS at least `100 * chains`. The reported Monte Carlo errors concern simulation error only.

References

Huang, A. and Wand, M. P. (2013). Simple marginally noninformative prior distributions for covariance matrices. Bayesian Analysis, 8, 439–452. doi:10.1214/13-BA815 .
